_doc: The self-enqueue chains reachable from a LiveViewTest trigger in the studio tree, each labelled with its HOP COUNT: the number of zero-delay self-messages the LiveView sends ITSELF between the handle_event the test triggers and the handle_info that writes to the store. Hop count is what decides how many barriers a test needs: `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.render/1` is ONE `GenServer.call(pid, {:phoenix, :ping})` (deps/phoenix_live_view/lib/phoenix_live_view/channel.ex, `def ping/1`), which orders only against messages ALREADY in the mailbox when it arrives. A 1-hop chain's send fires INSIDE the GenServer.call the trigger is already blocking on, so it is in the mailbox before the next ping and ONE barrier drains it deterministically. A chain of 2+ hops enqueues its next hop while the LiveView handles the previous one, AFTER the ping has been answered, so one barrier is not a drain and only a settle loop (ping until message_queue_len is 0, twice) is sound.
_sites: Each enqueue site is found by its code, not its line: `file` and the exact text `match` of the call (on a code line, not a comment), and `in`, the function it sits in. census_selftest.py C6 reds when a site's text no longer appears in its file.

CH-PAPEROP.terminus: api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/studio_live.ex handle_info({:paper_op, ...}) (both heads) -> Lifecycle.paper_op/2 -> Shared.paper_op/2 (store write). The handler issues no further self-enqueue.

CH-CHAT.terminus: api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/chat_live.ex handle_info({:dispatch_send, text, queued?}) -> ensure_session + wire write + persist. No further self-enqueue.

enqueue_sites.note: Phoenix.LiveView.Channel.send_update/3 -> send(pid, {:phoenix, :send_update, {ref, assigns}}) with pid == self()

CH-TREE.terminus: api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/studio_live.ex handle_info({:paper_op, ...}) (store write) — four generations after the trigger.
